summary: MariaDB is configured on node1 with the inventory database, items table, localhost-only application account, and protected credential file. Configuration and data survived a verified node reboot.
actions_performed: Installed, initialized, enabled, and started MariaDB 11.4.
Kept MariaDB socket-only with networking disabled.
Generated a 64-character credential from /dev/urandom on node1.
Created inventory_app@localhost with SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE privileges only on inventory.*.
Created /etc/inventory-db.env with root:root ownership and mode 0600.
Verified application authentication and database access.
Rebooted node1, confirmed its boot ID changed, and verified complete recovery.
Removed the temporary restart-persistence probe row.

evidence.summary: MariaDB is alive over /run/mysqld/mysqld.sock, skip_networking is enabled, no database TCP listener exists, and the service recovered after reboot.
Direct queries show the inventory schema, complete items table definition, InnoDB engine, and post-reboot persistence.

evidence.requirement: Local application account and generated credential
evidence.summary: Shows inventory_app@localhost, its limited CRUD grants, successful authenticated access, a redacted 64-character credential, and final account usability.
/etc/inventory-db.env is consistently root:root with mode 0600 before and after reboot.

Captures healthy baseline boot ID 53c34464-d13c-4133-b275-3b580597554b, reboot acknowledgement, changed boot ID 8d71d461-32b7-4be6-be9a-fdef483afd67, and recovered service, configuration, account, credential file, and persisted data.
